title: The client trusts any server key
ticket: CVE REPORT. A researcher shows our TLS client completes the handshake with a man-in-the-middle server whose ServerKeyExchange signature is random bytes. Valid servers still work and every test passes.
explanation: There are two goto fail lines in a row after the params hash. The first belongs to the if. The second is unconditional, despite the indentation, so execution always jumps to fail with err still TLS_OK from the successful hash update. rsa_verify is never called, so any signature is accepted. The tests only ever feed a valid signature, so they cannot catch it.

source.label: Adam Langley: Apple's SSL/TLS bug (goto fail), 2014
